text.p: The lira closed weaker at 105,530 against the dollar on Wednesday after Tuesday's 105,200 due to the dollar's gains against major currencies in world markets and banks' dollar demand.
Bankers said sellers were weak in the currency market which also caused the lira to slip after opening at 105,350.

The central bank set its dollar rate for banks' compulsory foreign currency transfers at 105,100 lira at the opening, after Tuesday's 105,000 lira close, and further raised it to 105,200 after the dollar's gains abroad.

The money market opened with a 6.4 trillion lira surplus. Overnight money traded between 77.25 and 77.75 percent during the day and the central bank lent 1.3 trillion lira at 78 percent overnight at close, up slightly from the 570 billion lira it funded at the same rate on Tuesday.

The central bank also fed banks 32.3 trillion lira via t/n value deals at 74 percent, up from the 28.1 trillion lira it funded on Tuesday. It also lent 1.7 trillion lira at 75 percent via tomorrow/week value deals.

Bond market yields eased around a point despite profit-taking. Yields had dived four to six points across the board on a buying spree prompted by strong demand and sharp yield cut in the Treasury's 13-month bond auction on Tuesday.
Treasury had sold 181.3 trillion lira of the 392-day bonds at 123.66 percent on Tuesday, down 12.66 points from the previous 9-month t-bill auction on December 3.
Bids had reached 478 trillion lira due to tax advantage of the papers having January 14, 1998 maturity, the longest so far. Corporate tax on interest gain from them will be paid in 1999.
Bankers said yields fell up two points at the opening, but firmed later in the day amid profit-taking sales.

The average yield on the most heavily traded January 14, 1998 paper, issued today, dropped to 109.71 percent from the auction yield of 110.82 percent (excluding witholding tax). The second most active October 30, 1997 paper yielded 111.05, down from Tuesday's 112.20 percent average.
